1. Balloons refer to the PARTS LIST. Arrangement and exploded views 1:2, Views A and B
1:1. Bracket figures are read from laser_bracket.scad at draw time. Jar, glove,
tripod, pack and lasers are bought parts drawn indicatively, not measured.
2. Cut a flat piece from a nitrile glove, stretch it drum-tight over the jar mouth and
hold the skirt below the lip. Even tension gives an even wibble.
3. Glue the 3 mirrors in a row across the centre, 23 apart to match the bracket, with the
row square to the tripod. Use a small dab: glue stiffens the glove.
4. Wrap the tripod legs round the jar neck below the lip. The clamp takes the pack; the
ball head tilts it so the bores point 45° down at the mirrors.
5. Lay the lasers in the bottom half with their leads in the grooves, close the top, pin
both hinges. The bores are 30 deep, so a 40 laser stands 10 proud at the back. How the
bracket fixes to the pack is not drawn.
6. Beams land at 45° and leave at 45° on the far side, 30 from laser face to mirror. When
the glove moves, a mirror tilted θ turns its beam 2θ, so the spots on the wall dance
7. Never look along a beam or its reflection. Aim the reflected beams at a wall away from
